# Canary

Updated: 2026-09-20

Version 3.9 adds a Go daemon client that runs the read-only tool catalogue
over the daemon socket, the statement performance series with dated flows and
year-to-date income, sector allocation under GICS with fund look-through at
market value, and a listing of every option held as portfolio protection. The
broker's "no security definition" answer is remembered instead of asked again,
and closed-market quote context no longer starves other history reads.
Broker-write gates are unchanged.

Canary is a local Interactive Brokers risk desk: a daemon, shell CLI, read-only
MCP server, paired app, and a public Go module with a daemon client and the TWS
wire protocol. The daemon
owns account scope, market sensors, rulebook evaluation, protection proposals,
option-exercise opportunities, and typed source quality. The CLI, MCP server,
and app are adapters over that authority.

Use it for:

- account, position, daily P&L, exposure, technical, and order-lifecycle reads;
- the Action Queue and daemon-composed daily brief;
- the 14-rule desk rulebook, operator-authored risk policy, and Flex-backed
  reconciliation;
- current option-strategy grouping, read-only protection proposals, and
  option-exercise opportunity review;
- explicit freshness, entitlement, source-health, warning-code, and session
  context; and
- Go programs reading the daemon through `github.com/osauer/canary/v2`, or
  building on the clean-room `pkg/ibkr` protocol package.

The MCP server exposes read-only tools for status, trading status, settings,
open orders, order history, one-order status, account, positions, option
strategies, named-symbol technical analysis, detailed regime and portfolio stress, brief, broker-reporting status and the
statement performance series, Edge, rules, proposals, opportunities, portfolio allocation, reconciliation status,
market quotes and price history, exchange sessions, and official macro calendars
and publications. It has no MCP resources, settings writes, order previews, or
execution tools. Breadth and gamma remain daemon inputs. Use
`canary_regime` for the eight-indicator market dashboard and `canary_stress` for
full portfolio-risk evidence; the daily brief remains the summary.

Standard downloads cannot place, modify, cancel, or exercise orders. A separate
opt-in `canary-trading` binary exposes constrained CLI and app order actions with
fresh confirmation/preflight, account and mode pins, journaling, daemon policy,
and the runtime freeze gate. Canary is not an automated trading system.

Product v3 releases ship as signed binaries, installer output, MCPB, and app
assets. The public Go module deliberately remains `/v2`; its `@latest` resolves
to the maintained v2 module line and does not install the product v3 binary.
